story.iWant: I want to fetch current odds for all available markets from the primary API source
story.soThat: edge calculation has accurate, fresh pricing data for all betting markets
story.tasks: - [ ] Task 1: Review API-Football odds endpoint structure (AC: #2, #3, #5) - [ ] Task 2: Implement fetch_odds() function (AC: #1, #2, #4, #5) - [ ] Task 3: Implement market-to-dict transformation (AC: #3, #4) - [ ] Task 4: Implement odds freshness validation (AC: #6, #9) - [ ] Task 5: Implement graceful degradation for missing markets (AC: #7) - [ ] Task 6: Implement odds validation (AC: #8) - [ ] Task 7: Implement error handling (AC: #12, #13, #14) - [ ] Task 8: Update API-Football fetcher module (AC: #1) - [ ] Task 9: Write unit tests (AC: #10, #11)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Implement `fetch_odds(fixture_id: str) -> Odds` function within `/src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/api_football.py` 2. Use API-Football's `/v3/odds` endpoint as primary source for all odds data 3. Fetch all available markets: match result (1X2), total goals (Over/Under 2.5, 3.5), corners, cards 4. Map API response to `Odds` model with nested `Market` objects containing outcome-to-odds mappings 5. Include `timestamp` field in response for freshness validation (extracted from API response) 6. Validate odds freshness: flag odds > 1 hour old as stale but continue processing (don't reject) 7. Handle missing markets gracefully: skip markets not available in API response (don't fail entire call) 8. Normalize all odds values: must be >= 1.0 (reject invalid odds) 9. Log odds age for each fixture (informational, not blocking) 10. Return `Odds` object with all available markets or raise appropriate exception on critical failure 11. All error handling follows CLAUDE.md patterns: custom exceptions, structured logging, graceful degradation 12. Handle 4xx errors: 404 → return None with warning log, 401/403 → raise APIAuthenticationError 13. Handle 5xx errors: raise APIServerError (will be retried by decorator) 14. Handle network/timeout errors: return None with warning log

doc.title: Technical Specification
doc.snippet: API-Football endpoints: fixtures, team statistics, injuries, odds. Rate limit: 300 req/min. Data quality: excellent for major leagues. Critical: handle nested response structures, respect rate limits.

doc.title: Data Dictionary
doc.snippet: Odds specification: bookmaker_name (Pinnacle, etc), odds_updated_at (ISO 8601), freshness requirement < 1h. Markets: match result (home/draw/away), total goals (over/under 2.5, 3.5), corners, cards. All odds >= 1.0. Timestamp for validation.

doc.title: Story 2.2: Integrate API-Football SDK
doc.section: Dev Notes - Learnings from Previous Story
doc.snippet: Story 2.2 provides: httpx.AsyncClient singleton, tenacity retry decorator (exp backoff 2-60s, max 5), RateLimiter class (token bucket, 100 req/min), custom exception hierarchy, structured logging, get_api_headers() function, rate limit handling with Retry-After header parsing.

doc.title: Story 2.4 (Current Story)
doc.section: Dev Notes - Architecture Alignment - API-Football Odds Endpoint Response Structure
doc.snippet: Endpoint: /v3/odds. Response structure: nested bookmakers → bets → values. Transform: extract update field (timestamp), extract bookmaker name, for each market transform values[] array to dict (outcome: odds), handle missing markets gracefully, validate odds >= 1.0.

artifact.reason: Pydantic models used in this story: Odds(fixture_id, bookmaker_name, odds_updated_at, markets[]), Market(market_type, odds dict). Models include validators for odds >= 1.0, non-empty strings.

artifact.reason: Story 2.2 provided: HTTP client singleton, retry decorator with exponential backoff (max 5 attempts, 2-60s), rate limiter token bucket (100 req/min), error handling (401/403/404/429/5xx), Retry-After header parsing. Story 2.4 will add fetch_odds() function in this module.

artifact.symbol: APIError, APIAuthenticationError, APIRateLimitError, APIServerError, DataValidationError, DataStaleError
artifact.reason: Custom exception hierarchy for error handling. Story 2.4 uses: APIAuthenticationError (401/403), APIRateLimitError (429), APIServerError (5xx), DataValidationError (invalid odds). See CLAUDE.md patterns.

Pattern examples for implementation: all three functions use fetch_with_rate_limit(), handle ValidationError gracefully (log + skip), return None on 404/timeout, raise exceptions on 401/403/5xx. Story 2.4 will follow identical pattern for fetch_odds().
Module exports: fetch_odds() must be added to __all__ export list after implementation

ecosystem.name: python
ecosystem.package: Async HTTP client with connection pooling

story-context.constraints: 1. MUST use existing HTTP client from Story 2.2 (get_http_client singleton, never create new clients) 2. MUST use tenacity retry decorator pattern from Story 2.2 (do NOT implement custom retry logic) 3. MUST use existing RateLimiter from Story 2.2 (api_football_limiter.acquire() before each request) 4. MUST use custom exception hierarchy from exceptions.py (APIAuthenticationError, APIServerError, etc.) 5. MUST follow Pydantic model validation patterns (don't ignore ValidationError) 6. MUST handle Retry-After headers for 429 rate limit responses (pattern from Story 2.2) 7. MUST implement graceful degradation (return None for 404/timeout, don't fail entire call) 8. MUST log all errors with context (URL, status code, fixture_id) using logger.error/warning/info 9. MUST validate odds values >= 1.0 (use Market validator, skip invalid outcomes) 10. MUST extract and preserve timestamp from API response for freshness validation 11. All error handling must follow CLAUDE.md patterns (structured logging, context, no bare except) 12. Response validation must use Pydantic models (not manual dict checking)

interface.name: fetch_odds()
interface.signature: async def fetch_odds(fixture_id: str) -> Odds | None
interface.description: Fetch current odds for all available markets from API-Football /v3/odds endpoint. Returns Odds object with timestamp and all available markets, or None for 404/timeout/network errors. Raises APIAuthenticationError (401/403) or APIServerError (5xx).

interface.name: get_http_client()
interface.description: Global HTTP client singleton. MUST be used for all API calls (don't create new clients). Already implemented in Story 2.2.

interface.name: RateLimiter.acquire()
interface.description: Token bucket rate limiter for API-Football (100 req/min). MUST call before each API request. Already implemented in Story 2.2.

interface.name: fetch_with_rate_limit()
interface.signature: async def fetch_with_rate_limit(url: str, api_name: str = "API-Football") -> httpx.Response | None
interface.description: Wrapper combining rate limiting + retry logic + error handling. Handles 401/403 (raise), 404 (return None), 429 (with Retry-After), 5xx (raise), timeout/network (return None). Already implemented in Story 2.2. Can be used directly or as pattern reference.

interface.name: Odds model
interface.signature: class Odds(BaseModel): fixture_id: str; bookmaker_name: str; odds_updated_at: datetime; markets: list[Market]
interface.description: Data model for odds with validators. Market objects contain market_type (str) and odds dict (str → float). All odds >= 1.0 enforced by validator.

interface.name: API-Football Odds Endpoint
interface.description: Returns nested structure: response[] → fixture, update (timestamp), bookmakers[] → id, name, bets[] → id, name, values[] → value (outcome), odd (decimal odds). Must handle missing markets, validate odds >= 1.0.

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio. All async functions use @pytest.mark.asyncio. Mock httpx responses with unittest.mock (AsyncMock, patch). Test data includes API-Football odds response samples. Assertions verify: model instantiation, field mapping, odds validation, error handling, graceful degradation. See tests/unit/test_api_football.py for examples (TestHTTPClient, TestRateLimiter classes).
